prompt: Sales is credited for new MRR, Customer Success for accounts that come back. For each month of 2025 (event_date from 1 January to 31 December 2025) with a new or reactivation event, give the new MRR and the reactivation MRR in euros. Each event's event_type names its movement (new, expansion, contraction, churn or reactivation); a reactivation is an account coming back after it churned, never new MRR. Leave out the opening events: they carry the MRR subscriptions already had when the data starts on 1 January 2024. Convert every amount to euros at one fixed rate, that of 31 December 2025: multiply by fx_rates.eur_per_unit for the subscription's currency on 2025-12-31. Count an event in the month of its event_date. A month with only one of the two shows 0 for the other. Round both to 2 decimals with ROUND. Return three columns, in this order: month_start (the first day of the month), new_mrr and reactivation_mrr. Return one row for each such month. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per month of 2025 with a new or reactivation event

hints: Next, write one conditional sum per movement: new events in one column, reactivation events in the other.
Each column adds only its own event_type, with 0 for the rest, so a reactivation never lands in new_mrr.
faded_shape:
WITH moves AS (
  -- one row per new or reactivation event in 2025, in euros
  SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', e.event_date) AS DATE) AS month_start, e.event_type,
    e.mrr_delta_local * f.eur_per_unit AS mrr_eur
  FROM subscription_events e
  JOIN subscriptions s ON s.subscription_id = e.subscription_id
  JOIN fx_rates f ON f.currency = s.currency AND f.rate_date = DATE '2025-12-31'
  WHERE e.event_type <> 'opening'
    AND e.event_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
    AND e.event_type IN ('new', 'reactivation')
)
SELECT month_start,
why_this_works: Each column sums its own event type, so a returning account is counted as a reactivation and never as new business.
